identity.title: Model Immunization from a Condition Number Perspective

problem.claim: Model immunization seeks pre-trained models that resist fine-tuning for harmful tasks while preserving utility on non-harmful tasks.

gap.claim: Prior work provided empirical evidence for text-to-image immunization, but when immunization is possible and how to define an immunized model precisely remained unclear.

contributions.claim: The authors propose a Hessian-condition-number framework for analyzing immunization in linear models.
They design a regularized algorithm intended to control condition numbers after pre-training.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish their approach by analyzing model immunization through Hessian condition numbers and using regularization to control them after pre-training.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report empirical results on linear models and nonlinear deep networks demonstrating the effectiveness of their algorithm for model immunization.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper frames immunization as retaining benign-task utility while hindering harmful-task fine-tuning.
It identifies unclear conditions for possibility and an imprecise definition as limitations of existing understanding.
It introduces a Hessian-condition-number framework and a regularized pre-training algorithm to control resulting condition numbers.
The authors report results on linear models and nonlinear deep networks supporting algorithm effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a formal quantity—the Hessian condition number—to both analysis and algorithm design, then reports evaluation across linear and nonlinear models.

lessons.interpretation: A measurable structural quantity can provide a bridge between explaining a mechanism and specifying an intervention.
lessons.application: When proposing a robustness method, define a tractable diagnostic quantity and state how the training objective is designed to control it, then test whether the claimed behavior appears beyond the motivating model class.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when the quantity lacks a defensible connection to the target behavior or cannot be estimated reliably in the intended setting.

unknowns: The abstract does not state the precise immunization definition, the conditions under which immunization is possible, or the quantitative results and baselines.
It does not specify which harmful and non-harmful tasks, datasets, metrics, or regularization terms were used.
Code availability is stated, but reproducibility details are not provided in the abstract.
